hypothesis: The three known taxi violations may be an artifact of the published canonical potential family: an arbitrary scalar potential on the finite frozen taxi graph may satisfy all difference constraints, or all but a controlled subset of the three residual edges.
rationale: Coefficient repair, full-coordinate additive repair, and published max/min envelope switches did not improve the verified three-violation candidate. The next separable diagnostic is the finite graph feasibility problem itself, which removes the potential-class restriction while retaining the exact frozen edge inequalities. Because a feasible value table would be benchmark-specific and potentially overfit, it is diagnostic evidence only.
expected_information_gain: Distinguishes a graph-level obstruction from failure of the tested canonical families. Feasibility after all three residual edges are removed can produce a finite candidate for the strict target screen; infeasibility, or feasibility only after exclusions, closes this arbitrary finite-potential route and requires a structured generalizing mechanism.
method: Load the pinned circle_taxi_k4_m6 metric and assign one free scalar variable to each of its 166,681 work-function nodes. Encode every retained taxi edge as Phi(v)-Phi(u) >= ext-(k+1)d_min, fix the first potential to zero, and solve sparse LP feasibility with five declared models: no residual edge removed, each of the three residual pairs removed, and all three residual edges removed. Use a 300-second HiGHS time limit per model and a 1,800-second total wall budget. Preserve every feasible value table with its full work-function rows. Any feasible table is independently array-checked on all taxi edges and then, only if it has fewer than three violations, sent through the pinned primary evaluator; no finite result is called a proof.
metric: frozen circle-taxi violations_k under the identical edge inequality; target is violations_k < 3
metric_relation_to_true_objective: This is a finite feasibility diagnostic on the pinned benchmark. A count below 3 is a strict improvement only for the frozen finite evaluator; arbitrary per-node values do not establish a general k-server potential or prove the conjecture.

configuration.variable_definition: one scalar per frozen taxi node/work-function row
configuration.solver: scipy.optimize.linprog method=highs with sparse two-nonzero rows

compute_budget.cpu: WSL2 pinned upstream runtime; sparse LP feasibility
compute_budget.memory_intent: one sparse constraint matrix at a time; no evaluator or metric changes

kill_condition: Stop after the five declared models, at 1,800 seconds total, or at a precise solver/runtime failure. Do not add edge exclusions, bounds, objective terms, or alternate solvers after seeing results. If no feasible model exists, close arbitrary finite difference-potential fitting. If a feasible model exists, independently count every taxi edge; only a count below 3 may trigger the pinned primary evaluator, and any finite value table must still be treated as overfit until a structured generalization is demonstrated.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: only a full frozen taxi count below 3 is strict finite improvement

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: this diagnostic removes the canonical-family restriction but is not itself a generalizing candidate

interpretation: All five declared sparse LP models reached the 300-second HiGHS limit without returning a primal solution. The finite graph feasibility question therefore remains unresolved; no infeasibility, feasibility, or objective improvement is claimed.
what_was_learned: Generic sparse LP is not an efficient certificate method for this 166,681-variable, 7,000,602-edge difference-constraint system under the available budget. The experiment does not distinguish graph-level obstruction from finite feasibility.
recommended_next_action: Use one bounded specialized difference-constraint relaxation/cycle-certificate diagnostic on exactly the same five edge-exclusion models; if it cannot produce a certificate within budget, close arbitrary finite fitting as computationally unproductive.
repetition_justification: This is not a repetition of additive feature repair or envelope switching: it removes the functional-family restriction and solves the frozen edge system directly with one variable per benchmark node.
